description: Benchmark prompts for ChatQEC's five core Stim-backed MCP tools (stim_simulate, stim_diagram, pymatching_decode, threshold_sweep, code_params) — companion to eval/lightstim_qec_prompts.json, same shape. Distinguishes prompts where a raw circuit is supplied in the prompt (reliable path) from prompts that require the model to hand-write a circuit for a named code (a documented weak spot — see docs/stim_getting_started_capability_check.md, which found stim_simulate/stim_diagram/pymatching_decode fail or silently produce wrong qubit counts on hand-rolled named-code circuits about half the time, while threshold_sweep/code_params — which call stim.Circuit.generated internally — are reliable). Not run in bulk; run a subset live and record raw logs the same way docs/lightstim_capability_check.md does.

categories.tool_simulate: stim_simulate with a raw circuit given in the prompt — reliable path
categories.tool_simulate_named: stim_simulate on a named code with NO circuit given — model must hand-write it; known weak spot
categories.tool_diagram: stim_diagram with a raw circuit given in the prompt
categories.tool_diagram_named: stim_diagram on a named code with NO circuit given — known weak spot
categories.tool_decode: pymatching_decode with a raw circuit given in the prompt
categories.tool_decode_named: pymatching_decode on a named code with NO circuit given — known weak spot
categories.tool_sweep: threshold_sweep — always named-family, generated internally via stim.Circuit.generated, reliable
categories.tool_edge_case: Should fail gracefully (ok=False or a clear rejection), not crash or silently return a wrong-shaped result
categories.combined: Should invoke more than one tool coherently

prompts.question: Create a simple 2-qubit Stim circuit that prepares a Bell pair (H on qubit 0, CNOT from 0 to 1) and measures both qubits in the Z basis. Simulate 2000 shots and show me the sampled measurement results.

reference.expected_outcome: every sampled row is [0,0] or [1,1], never [0,1]/[1,0] — perfect ZZ correlation

prompts.question: Simulate a distance-9 repetition-code memory circuit in Stim for 25 rounds and report the detector firing rate.
prompts.notes: Documented weak spot (capability-check #3): the model has previously hand-written a circuit that resets data qubits every round, destroying the memory, and reported an analytic estimate instead of a tool-derived aggregate (the tool only returns a sample preview, never an aggregate rate). Watch for both failure modes.

prompts.question: Render this Stim circuit as a timeline diagram: `H 0\nCNOT 0 1\nM 0 1`
Show me a Stim timeline diagram of a distance-3 rotated surface code memory circuit.
prompts.notes: Documented failure (capability-check #10): a prior run hand-rolled a 24-qubit (14 data + 10 ancilla) circuit — wrong; the true d=3 rotated surface code is [[9,1,3]], 9 data + 8 ancilla = 17 qubits total, confirmed by code_params in the same session. A correct answer either matches 17 qubits or routes through code_params/qec_circuit_build first to get the real layout before diagramming.

prompts.question:
MWPM-decode this Stim circuit over 5000 shots and tell me what fraction of shots have a logical error: `X_ERROR(0.05) 0 1 2
M 0 1 2
DETECTOR rec[-1] rec[-2]
DETECTOR rec[-2] rec[-3]
OBSERVABLE_INCLUDE(0) rec[-1]`
prompts.notes: Toy 3-qubit repetition-style circuit; verified directly against the tool: ok=True, logical_error_rate≈0.008 at p=0.05, 5000 shots (stochastic — expect close, not exact, on re-run).

prompts.question: Decode a distance-5 surface-code memory experiment at p=0.005 over 10,000 shots and give me its logical error rate.
prompts.notes: Documented weak spot (capability-check #5): 5 hand-written circuit variants attempted in one session, ended at confidence: low with no logical error rate ever reported. A correct answer should get a real number close to the reference in ls-cmp-style sanity checks (~0.005-0.02 range depending on rounds), or should fail over to threshold_sweep instead of giving up.

prompts.question: Sweep the physical error rate for the rotated surface code at distances 3 and 5, p in [0.02, 0.05, 0.10], and plot the logical error rate.

reference.note: Real numbers from docs/EXAMPLES.md's verified 2026-07-12 smoke-run (stochastic — expect close, not exact, on re-run)
reference.expected_pattern: below threshold (p=0.02): larger d wins (lower LER); above threshold (p=0.10): larger d loses

prompts.question: Find the threshold of the repetition code and show me the log-log plot.
prompts.notes: Correct answer explains the repetition code has no real QEC threshold (all sweep points show larger d losing, since there's only one error type it protects against) — capability-check #7 got this right.

prompts.question: For a distance-5 rotated surface code, report [[n,k]], the stabilizer count, and the code distance.
How many physical qubits encode one logical qubit in the distance-9 repetition code, and what's its distance?
What is [[n,k]] and the code distance for a distance-3 color code, and why might the reported distance be a lower bound?
prompts.notes: stim_code_distance (2) is the graphlike distance, a lower bound on the true distance (3) — color-code hyperedge errors are undercounted by shortest_graphlike_error. Correct answer explains this caveat, not just reports 2 as fact.

prompts.question: Report [[n,k]] and code distance for a distance-4 rotated surface code.
Sweep the surface code at distances 3, 5, 100 for p=0.05.
prompts.expected_outcome: ok=False — distance 100 is outside the tool's schema range [3, 15].

prompts.question: Report the distance-5 rotated surface code's parameters, then sweep its logical error rate at p=0.01, 0.05, 0.10 and tell me if it's below threshold at the lowest p.

reference.expected_pattern: below threshold at p=0.01 relative to a smaller distance's LER at the same p

prompts.question: Build me a distance-3 repetition code circuit, diagram it, and then decode it at p=0.1 over 2000 shots.
prompts.notes: Tests whether the model reuses ONE circuit across both tool calls consistently, or diagrams one hand-rolled circuit and decodes a different (possibly inconsistent) one.
